newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Firm oil price to power Enterprise.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Firm oil price to power Enterprise.

text.p: Surprisingly strong crude oil prices are seen giving a major boost to first-half results of Enterprise Oil, the production and exploration firm which reports on Thursday.
Analysts said oil and gas production growth will also have lent a helping hand.
Their forecasts for net income vary between 65 million stg and 80 million stg, compared with 46.5 million in the same period last year.
But the dividend is seen remaining unchanged at 6.5 pence.
Analysts said Enterprise is probably not yet convinced that oil prices will remain at their current high levels.

Crude, which seemed lacklustre at the begining of the year, rose in the first half of 1996 following severe winter weather, production delays in non-OPEC countries and a general demand increase as economies picked up.
Prices powered ahead further earlier this week as tensions in the Middle East flared up and the United Nations shelved a food-for-oil deal with Iraq.
Enterprise already said in May that its output rose in the first-quarter to 218,900 barrels of oil equivalent per day against an average 202,350 in 1995.
Enterprise main production area is the Nelson field in the North Sea, but the group also has promising activities in Italy.
Additionally, the company is also involved in Norwegian and Danish offshore projects which should come onstream in 1998.
"The higher oil price really suits them this year, because it is only in the next few years that we'll see production rise substantially," said analyst Jurjen Lunshof at Credit Lyonnias Laing.
